title: Void
body:
`void`. The absence of a type. A [[Function]] declared `void` returns nothing, so `return;`
with no value is legal and `return x;` is a [[Compile Errors|compile error]].

```c++
void print_header() {
	cout << "Name  Score" << endl;
	return;              // optional
}
```

A void function is the one place a function does its work through side effects instead of a
return value: printing, or writing through a [[Call by reference|reference parameter]]. A
C++ function returns at most one value, so any function that has to hand back two uses
reference parameters and is usually `void`.

`main()` is the exception that is not one: it returns `int`, always, even though nothing in
your program reads the result. See [[main()]].
